name: Karakol Centre
tagline: The Russian colonial grid, with the bazaar and the guesthouses
description: The town centre laid out on a grid by the Russian garrison in 1869, with single-storey wooden houses, carved window frames and poplar-lined streets. The bazaar, the guesthouses, the trekking agencies and the few cafes are all here, and the whole of it can be crossed on foot in twenty minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bazaar, the agencies and the guesthouses on foot
pros: Everything walkable, including the bazaar and the agencies
The trekking community concentrates here in season
cons: Dusty in summer and muddy in spring
Wooden houses are poorly insulated in winter
Very quiet outside the trekking season

name: Dungan Quarter
tagline: Around the wooden mosque built without nails
description: The northeastern quarter where the Dungan community, Chinese Muslims who fled to Kyrgyzstan in the 1870s, settled and built a mosque in Chinese temple style using no nails at all. The Dungan cafes here serve food quite different from Kyrgyz cooking and are the best eating in town.
bestFor: Stays that want the Dungan food and the town's most interesting quarter
pros: The Dungan mosque and the wooden Orthodox cathedral nearby

name: Karakol Valley and the Ski Base
tagline: Up the gorge towards the trailheads and the ski lifts
description: The valley running south from town into the Terskey Alatoo, holding the ski base, the trailhead for the Ala Kul route and a scatter of guesthouses among the pines. It is where anyone whose reason for being here is the mountains would sensibly stay, twenty minutes from the town.
bestFor: Trekkers and skiers who want the trailhead at the door
pros: Ala Kul trailhead and the ski base directly accessible
cons: Twenty minutes from town and its shops
Cold and isolated in deep winter

name: Issyk-Kul Shore and Pristan
tagline: Down at the lake, seven kilometres north
description: The lakeshore north of town, where Karakol meets Issyk-Kul, the second largest alpine lake in the world, which never freezes despite the winter. There are beaches, a small port area and guesthouses along the water. It is quieter than town and busy with Kazakh and Kyrgyz holidaymakers in July and August.
bestFor: Summer stays wanting the lake rather than the mountains
pros: Cooler air off the water in summer
cons: Busy with domestic holidaymakers in July and August

name: Jeti Oguz (28 km west)
tagline: The red sandstone valley and the hot springs
description: A valley west of Karakol below a wall of red sandstone formations called the Seven Bulls, with a Soviet-era sanatorium, hot springs and a broad grassy valley where herders bring animals up in summer and yurt camps operate. It is the classic Kyrgyz alpine meadow landscape.
bestFor: Stays wanting the summer pastures and the hot springs
pros: The Seven Bulls formation and the valley walks
Hot springs and yurt camps in season
cons: Transport is a shared taxi or nothing
Yurt camps operate only in summer
